avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Calcium competes with iron for absorption and can significantly reduce iron bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by at least 2 hours; prioritize iron dosing timing

avoid_supplements.name: Polyphenol-rich supplements (tea extract, grape seed extract)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Polyphenols chelate iron and reduce absorption
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; space administration by 2+ hours

avoid_supplements.name: Phosphate binders
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Can chelate iron and reduce systemic availability
avoid_supplements.action: Coordinate with dialysis team; separate dosing by 4+ hours if possible

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin C supplements (high dose >1000mg)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Excessive vitamin C may enhance iron absorption leading to potential iron overload
caution_supplements.action: Monitor ferritin levels; avoid megadosing; moderate supplementation acceptable

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May compete for absorption sites but effect is mild with IV iron
caution_supplements.action: No strict separation required; monitor for GI symptoms if combined

avoid_foods.name: High-calcium dairy products (consumed with oral iron)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Calcium binding reduces iron absorption; note: IV iron bypasses GI absorption
avoid_foods.action: Restriction less critical with IV iron; apply if any oral iron supplementation occurs

caution_foods.name: Tea, coffee, red wine (high tannins/polyphenols)
caution_foods.mechanism: Tannins chelate iron; minimal impact with IV administration but relevant if transitioning to oral
caution_foods.action: No restriction needed with IV sucrose; educate on timing if oral iron prescribed

caution_foods.name: Phytate-rich foods (whole grains, legumes, nuts)
caution_foods.mechanism: Phytates reduce iron absorption via GI tract; irrelevant for IV route
caution_foods.action: No dietary restrictions necessary with IV iron therapy

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum ferritin, TSAT (transferrin saturation), and hemoglobin regularly as IV iron sucrose bypasses GI absorption, eliminating most food/supplement interactions at absorption level. Assess for signs of iron overload (elevated ferritin >500 ng/mL) particularly in dialysis patients receiving frequent dosing.
